answer: Nodes first lock 64 gigabytes of unpageable DRAM into a dense trellis graph. Verifiers dispatch rapid sparrow probes, splitting pointer chains across memory banks like light through a prism. Provers must traverse these chained addresses within strict 75-nanosecond bus access budgets, preventing disk offload or remote relaying. Missed timing deadlines trigger immediate stake slashing and identity revocation. Fabricating 1000 concurrent identities requires 64 terabytes of dedicated physical memory costing over $19000 monthly.
